settingsTasks.title: Scheduled Tasks
settingsTasks.description: Manage background scheduling, target sessions, remote delivery and run results.

naturalLanguage.label: Draft a task in plain language
naturalLanguage.hint: This only produces a draft for you to review — nothing is created or started yet.
naturalLanguage.placeholder: e.g. summarize project progress every day at 9am

errors.intervalRange: The interval has to be between 1 minute and 1 year
errors.missingPrompt: Add what the task should actually do
errors.dailyNeedsTime: A daily task needs a time, for example "every day at 9am"
errors.onceNeedsTime: A one-off task needs a time, for example "tomorrow at 3pm"
errors.unsupported: Supported phrasings right now are "every 30 minutes", "every day at 9am" and "tomorrow at 3pm"

overview.needsAttentionHelper: Late, missed, or failed on the last run

list.title: Tasks
list.emptyDescription: Once you create a task, its schedule state and latest results show up here.

detail.emptyTitle: Pick a task to see its details
detail.emptyDescription: Task details cover the trigger time, health state, delivery settings and recent run history.
detail.noPrompt: This task has no prompt yet.
detail.nextRunStoppedHelper: Nothing triggers while the task is stopped
detail.heartbeatHelper: Time of the most recent scheduling activity
detail.aiCanExitHelper: The AI may end the loop task itself
detail.aiCannotExitHelper: The AI cannot end the task itself

runs.title: Recent runs
runs.emptyDescription: After the first run, results, errors and linked sessions appear here newest first.

toast.loadFailed: Could not load the scheduled tasks
toast.saveFailed: Could not save the scheduled task
toast.recoverFailed: Could not recover the missed runs
toast.toggleFailed: Could not switch the scheduled task state

scheduleEditor.title: Trigger type
scheduleEditor.everyHint: Repeat on a fixed interval in minutes
scheduleEditor.cronHint: Precise timing with a cron expression
scheduleEditor.atHint: Run once at a specific time
scheduleEditor.loopHint: Continue automatically after each run — good for autonomous flows
scheduleEditor.loopNotice: Loop mode keeps going after every run: 3 seconds after a success, and with a backoff delay after a failure. Best suited to long-running autonomous tasks.

editor.description: Set the task content, trigger time, target session and result handling.
editor.promptSummaryPlaceholder: A summary of the task prompt shows up here so you can check the whole task at a glance before saving.
editor.footerNotice: A scheduled task always runs with the permission mode you set here — it never inherits the approval state of the current foreground session.

content.title: Task content
content.description: The name and prompt define what this background flow is and what it should produce.
content.promptDescription: This is sent to the agent on every trigger.
content.promptPlaceholder: What should the agent receive when the task triggers?

schedule.title: Trigger time
schedule.description: Pick a fixed interval, a cron expression, a one-off trigger, or a continuous loop.

target.title: Target session and delivery
target.description: A new session suits recurring reports; a continuous session suits context that builds up over time.
target.newSessionHint: Create a fresh session on every run
target.singleSessionHint: Keep appending messages to the same session
target.projectPathDescription: New sessions use this directory as their project root.

runtime.title: Runtime and results
runtime.description: Runtime context, enabled tools and result handling all live in this column.
runtime.additionalDirectoriesDescription: One directory per line, added to this task's context scope.
runtime.enabledToolsDescription: Enabling only the tools this task really needs keeps its behavior predictable.
runtime.permissionModeDescription: Background tasks follow this mode strictly and never depend on the approval state of the current foreground session.
runtime.permissionModeHint: `auto` suits fully automated tasks; `smart` is the default interactive policy and suits background flows where sensitive operations should be approved.

result.title: Result handling
result.deliveryDescription: Deliver to several remote channel bindings at once. By default every delivery has to succeed for the remote delivery check to pass.
result.deliveryNoneDescription: Keep the result in the local session only.
result.noBindings: No remote channel bindings yet. Send a message from Telegram, Discord, Lark or WeChat to create one.
result.verificationDescription: Judges "the task ran" and "the output is good" separately — useful for daily reports, journals and backups.
result.replyNonEmptyDescription: Recommended for journal, report and summary tasks, so a run cannot succeed with an empty body.
result.bridgeDeliveryDescription: If the task depends on a remote channel to deliver the final result, make delivery part of the success condition.
result.fileExistsDescription: Good for backups, logs and file-writing tasks. Relative paths resolve against the current project root.
result.notifyMissedRunDescription: When a task misses its deadline, append a local system message — and send an alert too if a remote channel is configured.
result.aiCanExitDescription: Best kept for loop mode: it lets the model call the exit tool once the task is done.
